parsed.explanation: The combined regime layers a hostile federal document/entry regime (X and non-birth-sex markers barred, visa officers told to refuse on sex doubt and weigh lifetime fraud findings; passports blocked) onto a state that bars identity-congruent facility use in public buildings and schools, has no state anti-discrimination or gender-identity hate-crime coverage, bans under-18 transition care, and permits religious service refusal. Documented outcomes include a criminal trespass arrest with 24 hours in a men's ward, federal immigration-custody abuse, and a federal conversion-therapy policy for inmates. Protections (federal hate-crime and employment law, marriage, litigation, one successful settlement) are real but partial and unstable. Universal exposures with no working remedy dominate; no criminalisation of identity itself or death penalty caps severity.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 bar on X and non-birth-sex passport/visa markers, upheld Nov 2025; consular cable tells officers to refuse where documents cast doubt on sex and to weigh lifetime fraud ineligibility; travellers report passports blocked or seized; 8+ foreign governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid to expiry; ACLU suit pending; legal-aid FAQ on document rules; fraud finding requires four elements and is never automatic.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch → refusal/fraud inquiry → detention → birth-sex placement in custody.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented first bathroom-law arrest (trespass, up to 60 days) with 24h held in a men's ward; transgender men in immigration custody report forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse; federal corrections bureau from 2026 mandates hair-cutting, hormone removal and substituted psychiatric therapy for trans inmates; floor debate raised solitary placement for incarcerated trans people.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity; subject released on pretrial release; litigation ongoing.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility entry → arrest → birth-sex ward; visa discrepancy → immigration custody → documented abuse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; state 2025 law bars identity-congruent use in state buildings, schools and colleges (effective 1 July 2025), including off-campus activities; mapped bans reach private settings in 6 states; 4 states criminalise use in certain circumstances.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 states plus capital district have no mapped ban; a few municipalities give limited local protections.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal plus state bans jointly exclude the outed visitor from most public buildings entered.

care_services.exposure: State bans under-18 gender-affirming care (tapering ended Dec 2023, suits allowed to age 25); proposed federal rule barring public-insurance reimbursement for trans under-18; DOJ subpoenaed under-19 patient records; LGBTQ youth crisis line shut; 2021 law lets businesses deny goods/services to LGBTQ people on religious grounds.
care_services.protection: Emergency care refusal not documented; a state health secretary issued a written apology and paid $300k settlement after discriminating against an LGBTQ health contractor.
care_services.interaction: Travelling minor's care-seeking triggers provider liability and religious-refusal exposure for the whole family.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal orders call minors' care 'mutilation', direct law enforcement to investigate schools and prosecute teachers facilitating social transition, and freeze 'gender ideology' funding; Dec 2025 reward memo and May 2026 counterterrorism strategy name 'radically pro-transgender' ideology as a priority target category; 66% back birth-sex document rules.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Memo never lists the phrase as a reward criterion; strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target people who simply disagree.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises outing probability and emboldens state and street-level enforcement.

minors_guardians.exposure: State under-18 care ban with private right of suit; school facility ban covering off-campus activities; federal order threatening criminal referral against teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; sports and athletic participation bans.
minors_guardians.protection: Marriage and parental recognition not curtailed; no documented prosecution of a travelling parent.
minors_guardians.interaction: A visiting trans child's school or clinic contact can trigger state scrutiny, missed schooling or denied care.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: State hate-crime law does not cover gender identity and no state anti-discrimination law exists; only 23 states cover gender identity in bias statutes; travel guidance advises checking recent violence reports; documented handcuffing and public arrest of a trans woman.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime statute covering gender identity and 2020 national employment ruling supply a backstop; no documented pattern of trans killings in this dossier.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police call → state charge with no state bias coverage; federal bias charge remains possible.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Custody enforcement of the facilities law unresolved; driver's-licence gender-change status after the March 2026 birth-certificate ruling unconfirmed; several federal orders enjoined or contested, so exposure shifts with litigation; state lacks anti-discrimination and hate-crime coverage.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts demonstrated once (settlement, apology, $300k); pending constitutional challenges; running legal-aid FAQ; national employment and hate-crime backstops.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Stable paper protections versus actively contested federal orders create unpredictable exposure at travel time.

anchor_checks.comparison: Varnalia combines routine arrest for document mismatch with months of pretrial custody, coerced confessions, and near-illusory remedies. Here only one arrest is documented, custody lasted 24 hours with pretrial release, identity itself is not criminalised, and courts demonstrably worked once. No credible execution pathway exists. Materially safer than 0.15-A, so well above 0.15.

Vesskar shows universal checkpoint exposure, lengthy verification detentions, documented humiliation and denial of care, a narrow anti-discrimination claim, scarce legal aid, and inconsistent enforcement. This dossier matches that structure — universal document and facility exposure with thin state recourse — but adds a criminal trespass arrest, men's-ward holding, custody abuse and a minors' care ban. Slightly below 0.45-A.

Meridia lets visitors enter on marker-matching passports, trains border officers, offers tribunal appeal with compensation for unlawful detention, and keeps detention brief. This jurisdiction has the opposite document regime — markers frozen, refusal urged on sex doubt, possible lifetime fraud bar — plus facility exclusion and no comparable remedy. Far below 0.75-C.

Aldermere guarantees gender-affirming care, forbids disclosure without consent, and shows ombuds and licensing boards reversing refusals. Here minors' care is banned with a private right of suit, records were subpoenaed, and the youth crisis line was closed. The gap is decisive: care access runs in the opposite direction, so nowhere near 0.85.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets one system: a federal document and entry regime that freezes markers and invites refusal on any sex doubt, layered on a state that excludes trans people from public buildings and schools, bans minors' care, and offers no state anti-discrimination or bias-crime coverage. Discovery is likely at the visa desk, in a state building, or when a family seeks care. Outing consequences run from service refusal and facility exclusion (universal) up to trespass arrest with birth-sex ward placement, immigration-custody abuse, and federal inmate conversion-therapy policies. Protections are real but partial: federal hate-crime and employment law, marriage, pending litigation, and one demonstrated court win. Litigation volatility keeps the ceiling uncertain, but no working remedy yet offsets the operative exposures.
